items.content: Study of mathematical symbols and rules. Allows solving for unknown values. Foundation for higher mathematics.
Study of shapes, sizes, and properties of figures. Includes points, lines, angles, triangles, circles, and three-dimensional objects.
In right triangles: a² + b² = c². Relates the lengths of sides. Named after ancient Greek mathematician Pythagoras.
Study of change and motion. Includes derivatives (rates of change) and integrals (areas and accumulation). Foundation of physics and engineering.
Study of likelihood and chance. Ranges from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). Used in statistics and decision-making.
Study of vectors and matrices. Essential for computer science, physics, and engineering applications.
